title: OWASP Top 10 Web Application Security Risks
content: Use the OWASP Top 10 as a developer-focused map of critical web application risks. Study broken access control, injection, security misconfiguration, cryptographic failures, insecure design, vulnerable components, authentication failures, integrity failures, logging failures, and server-side request forgery. Connect each category to concrete code review checks, threat modeling questions, and remediation habits.

title: SQL Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet
content: Learn how SQL injection happens when untrusted data is mixed into dynamic queries. Practice using parameterized queries, safe ORM APIs, allow-list validation, least-privilege database accounts, and review patterns that reject string-built SQL. Focus on fixing findings that mention injection, tainted input, database queries, or unsafe command construction.

title: Input Validation Cheat Sheet
content: Build a habit of validating data at trust boundaries. Prefer allow-list validation, strict types, length limits, range checks, canonicalization, and central validation helpers. Apply this when findings mention unchecked user input, unsafe parsing, deserialization risk, missing validation, or high-risk request parameters.

title: Secrets Management Cheat Sheet
content: Learn how to keep secrets out of source code and logs. Practice environment-based configuration, managed secret stores, key rotation, access control, audit trails, and incident response for leaked credentials. Use this for findings involving hardcoded passwords, tokens, API keys, private keys, or insecure configuration.

title: Secure Coding Practices Quick Reference Guide
content: Use this as a broad checklist for secure implementation. It covers validation, output encoding, authentication, password management, access control, session handling, error handling, logging, data protection, communication security, system configuration, database security, and file management. Map security findings to repeatable coding practices.

title: unittest - Unit Testing Framework
content: Learn Python's standard unit testing framework: test cases, assertions, setup and teardown, test suites, and discovery. Use it to add targeted regression tests around changed logic, edge cases, security-sensitive validation, and bug-prone code paths when coverage or reliability metrics are weak.

title: pytest Documentation
content: Use pytest to write concise, maintainable tests with plain assertions, fixtures, parametrization, and discovery. Practice tests for boundary cases, validation rules, refactoring safety, security fixes, and behavior that previously had no coverage.

title: Coverage.py Documentation
content: Learn how to measure which Python code is exercised by tests, inspect missing lines and branches, and use coverage reports to guide meaningful test additions. This is useful when Sonar coverage is low, quality gates fail on coverage, or critical files lack regression tests.

title: Refactoring Techniques
content: Study practical refactoring moves for composing methods, moving features between objects, organizing data, simplifying conditionals, and reducing duplication. Apply these techniques to high-complexity files, repeated logic, oversized functions, and code smells reported by SonarQube.

title: Code Smells
content: Learn to recognize bloaters, object-orientation abusers, change preventers, dispensables, and couplers. Use code smell recognition to turn Sonar code smells into concrete refactoring decisions, especially when maintainability rating, technical debt, or code smell counts are weak.

title: Cognitive Complexity
content: Learn why deeply nested control flow, tangled conditionals, recursion, and hard-to-follow branches make code harder to understand. Practice flattening conditionals, extracting functions, using guard clauses, and separating responsibilities when cognitive complexity or complexity issues are high.

title: Clean as You Code
content: Learn the SonarQube practice of keeping new or changed code clean before trying to fix every legacy issue. Focus on quality gates, new-code conditions, maintainability, reliability, security, coverage, and duplication. Use this when Sonar quality gate status, code smells, coverage, or duplication need sustained improvement.

title: Managing Quality Gates
content: Use SonarQube quality gates to understand pass/fail conditions for maintainability, reliability, security, coverage, duplication, and new-code standards. Apply this when a repository has a weak quality gate, low test coverage, high duplication, bugs, code smells, or repeated quality standard failures.

title: Duplications Metric Definition
content: Learn how SonarQube reports duplicated blocks, duplicated lines, and duplication density. Use duplication metrics to decide where shared helpers, clearer abstractions, or test parametrization can reduce copy-paste maintenance risk without over-engineering.

title: Google Python Style Guide
content: Use a mature Python style guide to improve naming, module structure, imports, docstrings, exception handling, tests, and readability. This is useful when style violations, maintainability issues, inconsistent naming, or hard-to-review Python code appear in analysis.

title: Authorization Cheat Sheet
content: Learn practical authorization controls such as deny-by-default decisions, least privilege, centralized authorization checks, and server-side permission enforcement. Use this when findings mention broken access control, missing permission checks, insecure direct object access, role checks, or sensitive endpoint exposure.

title: Authentication Cheat Sheet
content: Study authentication implementation practices for login, password handling, account recovery, MFA, and attack resistance. Use this when recommendations mention weak authentication, insecure login flows, missing MFA, credential handling, session abuse, or account security.

title: Logging Cheat Sheet
content: Learn what security-relevant events to log, how to avoid leaking sensitive data, and how to make logs useful for detection and debugging. Use this when findings mention missing audit trails, poor observability, unsafe logging, exception handling, or incident response gaps.

title: Error Handling Cheat Sheet
content: Learn how to handle application errors without exposing stack traces, secrets, internal paths, or implementation details. Use this when findings mention verbose errors, unsafe exception handling, leaked debug information, or missing centralized error handling.

title: Managing Issues
content: Learn how to retrieve, review, triage, edit, and fix SonarQube issues. Use this when recommendations involve code smells, bugs, vulnerabilities, false-positive review, issue prioritization, or converting static analysis results into concrete fixes.

title: logging - Logging Facility for Python
content: Learn Python's standard logging module, logger levels, handlers, formatters, and structured logging habits. Use this when findings mention missing logs, print-based debugging, poor observability, exception tracking, or the need to avoid leaking sensitive values in logs.

title: Core Metadata Specifications
content: Learn how Python package metadata describes names, versions, requirements, classifiers, and project information. Use this when dependency findings require understanding package identity, dependency declarations, vulnerability scanner results, or supply chain metadata.

title: pip-audit: Python Dependency Vulnerability Scanning
content: Use pip-audit to scan Python environments and requirements.txt files for known vulnerabilities in direct and transitive dependencies. Practice running pip-audit against requirements.txt, reading CVE and advisory output, upgrading vulnerable packages, and confirming that vulnerable components are removed. This is directly relevant when findings mention vulnerable dependencies, outdated packages, vulnerable pytest versions, package CVEs, dependency management, requirements.txt, or Python supply chain security.

title: Safety CLI: Python Dependency Security Scanning
content: Use Safety CLI to detect vulnerable Python dependencies, malicious packages, and insecure package versions in local development and CI/CD. Learn how to scan dependency manifests, review remediation recommendations, upgrade vulnerable packages, and add dependency scanning to the delivery workflow. Use this for security recommendations involving vulnerable components, Python package risk, requirements.txt, dependency upgrades, and supply chain security.

title: OWASP A03:2025 Software Supply Chain Failures
content: Study how vulnerable, outdated, unsupported, or untracked third-party components create software supply chain risk. Learn to inventory direct and transitive dependencies, monitor CVE sources, apply risk-based upgrades, remove unused packages, prefer trusted sources, and build a patch management process. This is useful when analysis detects vulnerable components, outdated Python packages, unpinned dependencies, missing dependency scanning, or insecure requirements.txt management.

title: pip Requirements File Format
content: Learn the official requirements.txt file format used by pip to install Python dependencies. Practice declaring package versions, reviewing version pins, replacing unsafe or vulnerable versions, and keeping requirements files understandable and maintainable. Use this when findings mention requirements.txt, vulnerable package versions, dependency pinning, upgrade hygiene, or reproducible Python environments.

title: Python Packaging Version Specifiers
content: Learn how Python dependency version specifiers work, including exact pins, compatible release clauses, minimum versions, exclusions, and version ranges. Use this to replace vulnerable package pins with safe upgrade constraints, avoid accidentally allowing insecure versions, and document why a package version was upgraded. This is relevant for recommendations about requirements.txt pinning, vulnerable pytest versions, dependency upgrades, and Python package compatibility.

title: pytest Temporary Directory Fixtures
content: Learn how pytest temporary directory fixtures such as tmp_path and tmp_path_factory create isolated temporary paths for tests. Use this alongside dependency upgrades when findings mention pytest tmpdir, insecure temporary directory handling, unsafe test filesystem behavior, or Denial of Service risk. Practice writing tests that avoid shared predictable temporary paths and keep test artifacts isolated.

title: Denial of Service Cheat Sheet
content: Study Denial of Service risk from excessive resource usage, unavailable services, and missing resource controls. Learn mitigation habits such as setting limits, validating input size, applying timeouts, using rate limiting, isolating expensive operations, and monitoring availability. Use this when findings mention DoS, resource exhaustion, uncontrolled resource consumption, temporary directory abuse, or security weaknesses that can make an application or test workflow unavailable.

title: CWE-400: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption
content: Use CWE-400 to understand resource consumption weaknesses where software fails to track or restrict resource usage. Practice reviewing code and dependencies for missing limits, uncontrolled allocation, unbounded loops, unsafe temporary file or directory behavior, and operations that can exhaust CPU, memory, disk, or filesystem resources. This is relevant to Denial of Service recommendations and dependency vulnerabilities that impact availability.

title: CVE-2025-71176: pytest Temporary Directory Denial of Service
content: Review CVE-2025-71176 as a concrete example of how a vulnerable pytest version in requirements.txt can expose a project to Denial of Service risk through insecure temporary directory handling. Practice identifying the affected pytest version, checking the advisory, upgrading pytest to a safe patched version, updating requirements.txt, rerunning dependency scanning, and confirming that the vulnerable package version is no longer installed. Use this resource when recommendations mention Secure Coding, vulnerable pytest, pytest CVEs, DoS, tmpdir, temporary directory handling, or requirements.txt.

title: pytest Temporary Directory Fixtures: tmp_path and tmp_path_factory
content: Learn how pytest temporary directory fixtures work and how isolated temporary paths should be used in tests. Use tmp_path and tmp_path_factory to avoid unsafe shared temporary paths, reduce filesystem side effects, and improve test isolation. This resource is relevant when security findings mention pytest temporary directory handling, tmpdir, insecure temp directories, predictable temporary paths, DoS risk, or secure test practices.
